title: Sliding Window Token Bucket Rate Limiter
scenario: You are building an in-memory API gateway middleware at a high-volume fintech platform. Prevent abusive traffic per client IP without dropping legitimate bursts.
requirements: Implement class TokenBucket(capacity, refillRatePerSecond).
capacity is maximum tokens bucket can hold at any time.
refillRatePerSecond determines continuous token replenishment over elapsed time.
take(tokens = 1) returns true if enough tokens exist and consumes them; otherwise returns false without deducting.

testCases.description: Initial burst consumption within bucket capacity
Reject request when bucket is exhausted
Partial consumption preserves remaining tokens
testCases.input: bucket = new TokenBucket(10, 2); bucket.take(4); bucket.take(6); bucket.take(1);

hints.text: Track lastRefill timestamp and calculate elapsed time in seconds on each call to refill().
Replenish tokens with Math.min(capacity, tokens + elapsedSec * refillRate).

title: Promise Pool Concurrency Throttler
scenario: Your batch ingestion service needs to scrape 1,000 product pages, but the target server limits concurrent requests to 5 sockets. Implement an async task throttler that runs tasks with limited concurrency and preserves the original task result order.
requirements: Implement promisePool(tasks, limit) returning a Promise resolving to results in original task order.
tasks is an array of zero-argument async functions.
At most `limit` tasks must be running simultaneously at any given time.
If any task throws, reject immediately or propagate error correctly.

testCases.description: Executes 3 tasks with concurrency 2 in order
Empty tasks array resolves to empty array
Concurrency limit greater than task count

hints.text: Spawn `Math.min(limit, tasks.length)` worker functions that pull indices from a shared counter.
Preallocate `results = new Array(tasks.length)` and store each result at its original index.

title: Deep PII Data Sanitizer & Masker
scenario: Before pushing application logs to Datadog/Elasticsearch, all sensitive customer data (passwords, credit cards, CVVs, tokens) must be masked with '***REDACTED***'.
requirements: Implement maskSensitiveData(payload, sensitiveKeys).
Recursively traverse nested objects and arrays.
If an object key exists in sensitiveKeys (case-insensitive check), replace its value with '***REDACTED***'.
Do not mutate the original input object; return a clean deep clone.

testCases.description: Mask top-level password field
Mask nested array of authentication credentials
Case-insensitive key match: 'SECRET' and 'Cvv'

hints.text: Normalize sensitiveKeys into a Set of lowercase strings for O(1) comparison.
Handle primitive values, arrays, and objects separately to avoid recursion issues on primitives.

title: LRU Cache (Least Recently Used)
scenario: Implement an O(1) in-memory LRU cache to store resolved DNS records and database queries, evicting the least recently used entry when capacity is exceeded.
requirements: Implement class LRUCache(capacity).
get(key) returns the value if exists (updating usage to most recent), otherwise -1.
put(key, value) updates value if exists; if new, inserts it. If size exceeds capacity, evicts least recently used item.
Both operations must perform in O(1) average time complexity.

testCases.description: Basic put and get operations
testCases.input: cache = new LRUCache(2); cache.put(1, 1); cache.put(2, 2); cache.get(1);

testCases.description: Evicts least recently used key on overflow
testCases.input: cache = new LRUCache(2); cache.put(1, 1); cache.put(2, 2); cache.put(3, 3); cache.get(1);

testCases.description: Accessing key updates freshness and preserves it from eviction
testCases.input: cache = new LRUCache(2); cache.put(1, 1); cache.put(2, 2); cache.get(1); cache.put(3, 3); cache.get(2);

hints.text: JavaScript's `Map` retains insertion order: `.keys().next().value` returns the oldest inserted key.
When getting an existing key, delete it and immediately re-set it to move it to the end of insertion order.

title: Debounce Function with Immediate & Cancel
scenario: A fast search input on the candidate job board fires API requests on every keystroke. Implement debounce with support for immediate invocation and manual cancellation.
requirements: Implement debounce(fn, waitMs, options = { immediate: false }).
Delays invoking fn until waitMs milliseconds have elapsed since the last time it was invoked.
If immediate is true, trigger fn on leading edge instead of trailing.
Returned function must have a .cancel() method that cancels pending execution.

testCases.description: Fires only once after trailing delay
testCases.input: Calls debounced 5 times in 10ms with wait 50ms

testCases.description: Immediate flag executes immediately on leading edge
Cancel method stops pending execution

hints.text: Store the timer id in a closure and clear it whenever the debounced function is invoked again.
If immediate is true, call fn immediately when timer is null, then start the cooldown timer.

title: Deep Clone with Circular Reference Support
scenario: A state machine snapshot serializer crashes with 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded' when cloning cyclic state graphs. Build a resilient deep cloner.
requirements: Implement deepClone(value, seen = new WeakMap()).
Clones nested objects, arrays, Dates, and RegExps.
Handles circular references by reusing cloned references stored in WeakMap.
Preserves primitives unchanged.

testCases.description: Deep clone nested object without reference sharing
testCases.input: obj = { a: { b: 2 } }; clone = deepClone(obj); clone.a.b = 99; obj.a.b;

testCases.description: Handle circular reference without infinite loop
testCases.input: obj = { name: 'cycle' }; obj.self = obj; clone = deepClone(obj); clone.self === clone;

testCases.description: Properly clones Date and RegExp instances
testCases.input: clone = deepClone({ d: new Date('2026-01-01'), r: /abc/g }); clone.d instanceof Date;

hints.text: Use a WeakMap to map original object references to their cloned copies.
Set `seen.set(value, copy)` BEFORE recursively processing child properties to resolve cyclic references.

title: Type-Safe Event Emitter with Once & Off
scenario: You are building the real-time event distribution layer for live coding multiplayer rooms. Build a standalone event bus without Node.js EventEmitter dependencies.
requirements: Implement class EventEmitter.
on(eventName, listener): registers listener, returns unsubscribe function.
emit(eventName, ...args): invokes all registered listeners with args.
off(eventName, listener): removes specific listener.
once(eventName, listener): executes listener once and automatically unregisters.

testCases.description: Emits events with arguments to registered listeners
testCases.input: em = new EventEmitter(); em.on('msg', x => val = x); em.emit('msg', 'hello'); val;

testCases.description: Once listener executes only on first emit
testCases.input: count = 0; em.once('ping', () => count++); em.emit('ping'); em.emit('ping'); count;

testCases.description: Unsubscribe returned from on() removes listener

hints.text: Use a `Set` for each event in a Map to prevent duplicate registrations and enable fast deletion.
In `once`, create a wrapper function that calls `this.off` right before invoking the original listener.

title: Async Retry with Exponential Backoff & Jitter
scenario: Downstream payment webhook calls fail intermittently due to network blips. Implement resilient retry logic with exponential backoff and randomized jitter to avoid thundering herd.
requirements: Implement retryWithBackoff(fn, options).
options: { maxRetries: 3, baseDelayMs: 100, maxDelayMs: 2000, jitter: true }.
Delay between attempt n (0-indexed) is min(maxDelayMs, baseDelayMs * 2^n).
If jitter is true, multiply delay by random factor between 0.5 and 1.5.
If all attempts fail, reject with the error from the final attempt.

testCases.description: Resolves immediately on first attempt without retrying
Succeeds on 2nd retry attempt after failure
Throws final error when all retries are exhausted

hints.text: Loop from 0 to maxRetries. Catch error, check if attempt === maxRetries, otherwise compute delay.
Formula: `Math.min(maxDelayMs, baseDelayMs * (2 ** attempt))`.

title: Circuit Breaker Resilience Pattern
scenario: Protect microservices from cascading failures when an external identity provider goes down. Open the circuit breaker after consecutive failures, fast-failing subsequent calls.
requirements: Implement class CircuitBreaker(fn, options).
options: { failureThreshold: 3, cooldownMs: 1000 }.
States: CLOSED (normal), OPEN (fast-fail, throw CircuitBreakerOpenError), HALF_OPEN (trial request).
Transition from CLOSED -> OPEN when consecutive failures reach failureThreshold.
Transition from OPEN -> HALF_OPEN after cooldownMs elapsed. If trial succeeds -> CLOSED; if fails -> OPEN.

testCases.description: Executes successfully in CLOSED state
Trips to OPEN state after consecutive failures
testCases.input: cb = new CircuitBreaker(() => { throw new Error('ERR'); }, { failureThreshold: 2 });
testCases.expected: Throws 'Circuit Breaker is OPEN' on 3rd attempt

testCases.description: Enters HALF_OPEN state after cooldownMs and recovers on success

hints.text: Check if state === 'OPEN' and Date.now() >= nextAttempt; if so, transition to 'HALF_OPEN'.
On success, always reset failures = 0 and state = 'CLOSED'.

title: Nested Comment Thread (Flat to Tree Converter)
scenario: Database returns a flat SQL result of comments with parent_id pointers. Convert this flat list into a hierarchical Reddit/HackerNews-style comment tree in O(N) time.
requirements: Implement flatToTree(comments).
Each comment has { id, parentId, text }.
Root comments have parentId === null.
Each tree node should have a children: [] array containing its direct replies.
Must run in O(N) time without quadratic nested loops.

testCases.description: Convert single root comment with one child
testCases.input: flatToTree([{ id: 1, parentId: null, text: 'Hi' }, { id: 2, parentId: 1, text: 'Reply' }])
testCases.expected: [{ id: 1, parentId: null, text: 'Hi', children: [{ id: 2, parentId: 1, text: 'Reply', children: [] }] }]

testCases.description: Multiple root comments
testCases.input: flatToTree([{ id: 1, parentId: null }, { id: 2, parentId: null }])

testCases.description: Empty input produces empty array

hints.text: First pass: populate a Map from comment.id to a clone with children: [].
Second pass: if parentId is null push to roots, else find parent in Map and push to its children array.

title: Concurrent JWT Refresh Queue Manager
scenario: When a JWT access token expires, multiple parallel UI widget requests trigger simultaneous refresh calls, causing race conditions and revoked session tokens. Implement a request deduplicator queue.
requirements: Implement class TokenRefreshManager(refreshFn).
getValidToken(): returns active token.
refreshToken(): triggers token refresh. If a refresh is already in-flight, return the same promise to all callers.
All waiting callers resolve with the new token once refresh finishes.

testCases.description: Returns existing cached token if available
Deduplicates 3 concurrent refreshToken calls into 1 execution
testCases.expected: refreshFn called exactly 1 time, all 3 resolve to same token

testCases.description: Subsequent refresh after completion triggers fresh call

hints.text: Store the ongoing Promise in `this.refreshPromise`. If not null, return it immediately.
Use a finally block to reset `this.refreshPromise = null` when the promise completes or fails.

title: High-Performance Memoize with Custom Key & TTL
scenario: Expensive SVG chart rendering functions recalculate identical layouts on every window scroll. Build an in-memory memoizer supporting multi-argument hashing and TTL expiration.
requirements: Implement memoize(fn, { keyResolver, ttlMs } = {}).
keyResolver: custom function (...args) => string. Defaults to JSON.stringify(args).
ttlMs: optional time-to-live in milliseconds; if expired, recomputes fn.
Returns a wrapped function with a .cache clear method: wrapped.clearCache().

testCases.description: Caches identical call arguments
testCases.input: calls = 0; fn = memoize(x => { calls++; return x * 2; }); fn(5); fn(5); calls;

testCases.description: Differentiates different arguments
clearCache resets cached values

hints.text: Store an object `{ value, timestamp: Date.now() }` in the cache Map.
Check if `ttlMs` is defined and `now - entry.timestamp >= ttlMs` to evict stale entries.

title: Middleware Onion Pipeline (Express/Koa Compose)
scenario: Implement Koa and Express-style async middleware execution pipeline where middleware functions wrap each other in an 'onion' model calling await next().
requirements: Implement compose(middlewares).
middlewares is an array of functions fn(context, next).
Calling await next() transfers control to the next middleware in chain.
When downstream completes, control unwinds back through upstream middlewares.
Calling next() multiple times in the same middleware must reject with an error.

testCases.description: Executes middlewares in onion order
testCases.input: ctx = []; fn = compose([async (c, n) => { c.push(1); await n(); c.push(3); }, async (c, n) => { c.push(2); }]); await fn(ctx); ctx;

testCases.description: Rejects if next() is called twice in same middleware
testCases.input: compose([async (c, next) => { await next(); await next(); }])({})

testCases.description: Empty middleware pipeline resolves smoothly

hints.text: Maintain an `index` pointer to prevent multiple dispatches of the same index.
Wrap the invocation in `Promise.resolve(fn(context, () => dispatch(i + 1)))` to handle both async and sync middlewares.

title: Deep Object Equality Checker
scenario: React components need to prevent unnecessary re-renders without importing the heavyweight lodash.isEqual bundle. Implement a performant deep equality checker.
requirements: Implement deepEqual(a, b).
Returns true if both inputs are deeply identical, false otherwise.
Handles primitive values (numbers, strings, booleans, null, undefined, NaN).
Handles nested objects and arrays of arbitrary depth.
Handles Date instances by comparing timestamp.

testCases.description: Compares deeply nested objects
Detects subtle differences in nested array
Compares NaN correctly (Object.is)

hints.text: Use `Object.is(a, b)` first to handle identical references and NaN.
Compare `Object.keys(a).length === Object.keys(b).length` before iterating keys.

title: Virtual DOM Object Diff Engine
scenario: Build a lightweight DOM reconciliation engine that compares two virtual DOM node trees and outputs minimal change patches.
requirements: Implement diff(oldNode, newNode).
Nodes have shape: { type: string, props: {}, children: [] }.
If newNode is null/undefined, return patch { type: 'REMOVE' }.
If oldNode.type !== newNode.type, return patch { type: 'REPLACE', node: newNode }.
If props changed, output patch { type: 'UPDATE_PROPS', props: diffProps }.
Recursively diff children array and attach child patches.

testCases.description: Detects node type replacement
Detects updated and removed props
testCases.input: diff({ type: 'div', props: { className: 'btn', id: 'old' } }, { type: 'div', props: { className: 'btn-active' } })
testCases.expected: props contains className: 'btn-active' and id: undefined

testCases.description: Detects removed child node
testCases.input: diff({ type: 'ul', children: [{ type: 'li' }] }, { type: 'ul', children: [] })
testCases.expected: child patch type REMOVE at index 0

hints.text: Handle base cases: node missing, node type changed, or both nodes match.
Compare keys in newProps against oldProps, setting missing keys to undefined.

title: Query String Parser & Serializer
scenario: Single-page application search filters need to synchronize with browser URL query strings without loading heavy third-party packages.
requirements: Implement parseQuery(queryString) and stringifyQuery(params).
parseQuery parses '?a=1&b=hello&c=true' into { a: '1', b: 'hello', c: 'true' }.
Handles duplicate keys as arrays: '?tag=js&tag=react' -> { tag: ['js', 'react'] }.
Handles URI component decoding and encoding properly.
Omits null and undefined values in stringifyQuery.

testCases.description: Parse query string with encoded spaces and symbols
Parse repeated keys into array
Stringify object with array and omit null

hints.text: Strip leading '?' if present, then split by '&'.
Use `decodeURIComponent` and `encodeURIComponent` on every key and value.

title: Schema Validator & Error Reporter
scenario: Validate incoming user registration request payloads before hitting database models, returning clear validation error messages.
requirements: Implement validateSchema(payload, schema).
schema defines rules for keys: { type: 'string'|'number'|'boolean'|'array'|'object', required: boolean, min?: number, max?: number }.
Returns { valid: boolean, errors: string[] }.
If a required field is missing or null, report 'Field <key> is required'.
If type mismatches, report 'Field <key> must be of type <type>'.

testCases.description: Valid payload passes with no errors
testCases.input: validateSchema({ name: 'John', age: 25 }, { name: { type: 'string', required: true }, age: { type: 'number', min: 18 } })

testCases.description: Missing required field produces error
testCases.expected: { valid: false, errors: ['Field email is required'] }

testCases.description: Type mismatch produces error
testCases.expected: { valid: false, errors: ['Field age must be of type number'] }

hints.text: Check required fields first: `val !== undefined && val !== null`.
Watch out for `Array.isArray(val)` because `typeof []` is `'object'` in JS.

title: Priority Task Queue with Worker Slots
scenario: A PDF invoice processing service must process high-priority enterprise invoices before lower-priority free tier requests, capped at 3 worker slots.
requirements: Implement class PriorityQueue(concurrency).
add(taskFn, priority = 0): returns Promise that resolves when taskFn completes. Priority 10 is higher than 1.
Tasks with higher numeric priority must be executed before lower priority tasks.
Never run more than concurrency tasks concurrently.

testCases.description: High priority task jumps ahead in queue
testCases.input: pq = new PriorityQueue(1); pq.add(taskA, 1); pq.add(taskB, 1); pq.add(taskC, 10);

testCases.description: Never exceeds concurrency limit
Propagates task rejections correctly

hints.text: Sort the queue descending by `priority`: `(a, b) => b.priority - a.priority`.
In the `finally` handler of each task, decrement `this.running--` and call `this._next()`.

title: Reactive Observable State Store
scenario: Implement a minimal Redux/Zustand style state container with action dispatching, state subscriptions, and state selector caching.
requirements: Implement createStore(reducer, initialState).
getState(): returns current state.
dispatch(action): applies reducer(state, action), updates state, and notifies listeners.
subscribe(listener): registers listener, returns unsubscribe function.
select(selectorFn, listener): fires listener only when selectorFn(state) changes.

testCases.description: Dispatches action and updates state
testCases.input: store = createStore((s, a) => a.type === 'INC' ? s + 1 : s, 0); store.dispatch({ type: 'INC' }); store.getState();

testCases.description: Subscribed listener receives notification on dispatch
testCases.input: called = false; store.subscribe(() => called = true); store.dispatch({ type: 'INC' });

testCases.description: Unsubscribe stops notifications

hints.text: Keep `listeners` in a Set and notify all listeners on each dispatch.
For `select`, compare `nextSlice !== currentSlice` before invoking the callback.

title: Batch Request Debouncer (DataLoader Pattern)
scenario: GraphQL resolvers request user profiles by ID individually, causing the N+1 database query problem. Implement a batch coalescer that aggregates individual requests within the same tick into a single batch database query.
requirements: Implement class BatchDataLoader(batchFn).
load(key): returns a Promise that resolves with the value for that key.
Collects all load(key) calls made in the same event-loop microtask tick.
Calls batchFn(keys) once with unique keys, then resolves each individual Promise with its corresponding value.

testCases.description: Coalesces 3 concurrent load() calls into 1 batch call
testCases.input: batchCalls = 0; loader = new BatchDataLoader(async keys => { batchCalls++; return keys.map(k => 'user_' + k); }); Promise.all([loader.load(1), loader.load(2), loader.load(3)]);

testCases.description: Resolves correct corresponding value for each key
Propagates batch failure to all waiting callers
testCases.input: failingLoader = new BatchDataLoader(() => Promise.reject(new Error('DB_DOWN'))); failingLoader.load(1);

hints.text: Use `Promise.resolve().then(() => this._flush())` to schedule the batch flush on the microtask queue.
Drain `this.queue` into a local batch array inside `_flush()` and reset `this.scheduled = false`.
